title: File tool results the model reads are capped where the measured tail is: grep 100 matches and 1,000-byte previews, bash lines at 2,000 and outputs at 12,000 with the whole output kept in the session's spill file; read keeps dsh's own caps
steps: S1: No stand, no browser, no model. Work in the TCH checkout at the commit under test, with its dependencies installed (pnpm install) and the deepseek-harness submodule initialised.

S2: From the checkout root run: node --test --test-reporter=tap scripts/test/file-tool-caps.test.mjs packages/tools/tracy-subprocess-docker/test/output-bound.test.mjs — keep the 'ok'/'not ok' lines and the exit code.
expect: S2: every test named in run.tests reports ok. Both bundles' twelve presets set tool-fs-search grepMaxMatches 100 and grepMaxLineBytes 1000 (sampleOverCapGlobResults false kept), each a field dsh's tool still declares and lower than its default; no preset sets a read cap on tool-fs (readMaxLineLength, readMaxBytes, readLimit stay dsh's: a 1,000-character line cap was reverted in review because read cannot page inside a line, Writer and SEO/GEO have no shell to reach the rest, and a whole-file write rebuilt from a cut line would corrupt the file); no Tracy file overrides dsh-base's spill-policy (maxInlineTokens 12500). A bash output within 2,000 characters a line and 12,000 in all is untouched; a longer line keeps its start and its length; a longer output keeps its head and tail by whole lines and counts the rest; the exit/timeout markers stay last; the whole output is saved through the spill store under the session and call, and the notice names its file and how to print one part of a long line; with no store, a failing store or no session nothing is cut; other tools, program sub-calls, value replacements and image results pass untouched; the provider registers the bound on tools/post-execute.

selectors.presets: scripts/gen-presets.ts rowLines (tool-fs-search; tool-fs keeps dsh's defaults) -> packages/bundle/tracy-{cowork,native}/presets.patch.yml

evidence: Harness profile 09/10/2026 (candidate 8): tool results carried to later steps are 27-29% of all prompt tokens. Simulated on 1,980 bench sessions (24/09-05/10/2026): bash 55 of 2,255 calls cut, 696k of 4.07M characters (17%); grep 54 of 434 calls, 255k characters (21.5%, 27% carried); read 14 of 565 calls, 43k characters (1.7%), dropped in review. bash and grep together: about 4.4% of all carried tool-result characters.
fence: Mechanism only: what the model is shown of a file tool or bash result, that the whole bash output is saved first and nothing is cut when it cannot be. Not covered: whether a model then needs one more call to reach what was left out (a bench measure, flaky by nature).

tests: every preset of both bundles that mounts a file tool sets its cap
read keeps dsh's own caps in every preset: a long template line stays readable whole
grep still keeps its glob setting next to the new caps
each cap is a field dsh's tool reads, lower than dsh's own default
Tracy leaves dsh-base's spill-policy cap alone
the caps are the measured ones
an output within both caps is left as it is
a minified line keeps its start and its length
a cut never splits a surrogate pair
a long output keeps its head and its tail by whole lines
the status markers stay the last lines, after the notice
the notice names the saved file
boundBashResult saves the WHOLE output under the session
the content dsh accepted is read when the decision carries none of its own
no store, a failing store, or no session: nothing is cut
other tools, program sub-calls, value replacements, blocks and images pass untouched
the provider registers the bound on tools/post-execute
